summary: Jean-Baptiste Biot was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields who studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand, École Polytechnique, and École des Ponts ParisTech. He held professorships at École Centrale de Beauvais, Collège de France (1800–1862), and the Science Faculty of Paris.

Jean-François Jarrige worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Lycée Claude Fauriel, the École du Louvre, and the University of Paris, he served as director and head of the Guimet Museum from 1986 to 2008.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the University of Paris, and Paris Nanterre University. He held posts at the University of Paris, Paris Nanterre, Paris 8 (1972–1987), UC Irvine, and Emory University.
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, Lycée du Parc (~1941–1943), and École Normale Supérieure (1943).

Jean-Louis Burnouf studied at Lycée Saint-Louis and under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as professor of rhetoric at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, held the chair of Latin eloquence at Collège de France (1816–1844), and taught at the University of Paris.
Jean-Luc Achard works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2003–2004).

Jean-Luc Chevillard is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli. He held posts as a researcher at the CNRS (~1993) and as a lecturer at the University of Hamburg (~2003).

Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied under Bernard Frank and at INALCO. He held posts at the CNRS, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France (2011–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a Sinologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and at INALCO. He held the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Burgundy, INALCO, and under Yves Hervouet. He served as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1999–2004).

Jeannine Auboyer specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at the École du Louvre, EPHE, and University of Paris under mentors including Hackin, Grousset, and Stern. She was chief curator at the Guimet Museum and taught at the École du Louvre.

Jeff Dolven studied at the University of Oxford and earned a PhD from Yale University. He held posts as a junior fellow at Harvard University (~1996–1999) and later became a professor of English at Princeton University (~1999).

Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. He headed the philosophy programme at Murdoch University (~1989–1999) before becoming a professor and Emeritus Distinguished Professor at the University of Tasmania.
Jeff Shore is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who held posts as professor and professor emeritus at Hanazono University (attested 2001, 2026).
Jeff Watt works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.
Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under Taitetsu Unno and Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed degrees at the University of Notre Dame and the University of Chicago, later joining Elizabethtown College in 2000 as associate professor of religion and Asian studies.

Jeffrey Broughton specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1975 and held a post as professor of religious studies at California State University, Long Beach (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff studied at Missouri State University and UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White, Barbara A. Holdrege, and William F. Powell. In Indology and religious studies, his posts included instructor at Missouri State and assistant professor at Marshall University.
Jeffrey Davis Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), studying under Collett Cox and Sanghasen Singh.
